subject: Serving-mode transition options & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finapps.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>; Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sabrina Cole <sabrina.cole@finapps.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's demo

Hi Mina / Marcus,

Thanks for the demo this morning — appreciated the walkthrough of Redwood's routing and cache features. A few of us regrouped and want to be explicit about the migration considerations so we can pick a serving path: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem. High level context on our side:

- We run a legacy GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100) behind an internal API gateway; nightly fine-tuning and a small set of production endpoints.
- Peak traffic: roughly 90 TPS across ~10k daily active users, typical seq len ~1k tokens for retrieval-augmented responses.
- Data residency requirement: some PII must remain in our cluster (vendor compliance constraints) but models can be hosted elsewhere if retrieved content stays inside our VPC.

Primary questions after the demo:
1) For a lift-and-shift from our cluster to Redwood Dedicated, what is the expected rework on model packaging/serialization (we use a custom fork of an open LLM)?
2) If we try Hosted first as a low-friction PoC, how do you handle KV/prefix cache compatibility and latency expectations for ~90 TPS?
3) For Private VPC, what parts of the control plane remain customer-managed vs Redwood-managed?
4) Any recommended phased migration plan that minimizes downtime for nightly fine-tuning?

Attached are our post-demo notes and a short list of compliance constraints. Happy to sync tomorrow or early next week — Sabrina and I are available Mon/Tue afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Garcia
Head of Platform Engineering, FinApps

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finapps.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo

Alex — thanks for the clear context and the notes. Quick read and some clarifying Qs so we can recommend the best initial path:

- Packaging: when you say "custom fork of an open LLM," can you confirm whether you control the model weights and inference graph export (PyTorch .pt, HuggingFace format, or ONNX)? If so, Dedicated -> Private is straightforward. If the model is behind a provider API, that's a different path.

- Traffic shape: the 90 TPS — is that steady or spiky (e.g., 90 sustained vs bursts to 250 for seasonal events)? Also, how many concurrent sessions rely on long KV caches (average cached length)?

- Fine-tuning cadence: nightly; how long does your training + push-to-prod window take? Is zero-downtime deploy required for model swaps?

Initial recommendations based on what you shared:
1) Quick PoC (2–3 weeks): Hosted API using a compatible open model variant and synthetic traffic that mimics your seq lengths. This gives latency baselines and lets you validate RAG integrations without touching your infra.
2) Scale & throughput validation (4–6 weeks): If latency/throughput meet SLOs, move to Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity). We'll mirror your traffic pattern; minimal model repackaging required if you can provide weights in HF/PyTorch.
3) Private VPC (6–10 weeks): For PII residency, we deploy a customer-managed VPC with our private control plane. Control plane interactions (rollouts, metrics reporting) go over a managed control channel; data plane stays in your network.

I'm attaching a short one-pager that summarizes the differences and tradeoffs (redwood-serving-options-cheatsheet.pdf) plus our SOC2 evidence checklist so we can pin the compliance questions.

Next steps I propose:
- Can you confirm model artifact ownership/format and whether you can share a representative model (or a small distilled variant) for the Hosted PoC? (Action: Alex — by Mon 10/26)
- Marcus will draft a tentative Dedicated capacity sizing based on the burst profile (Action: Marcus — by Tue 10/27).
- We'll propose two timeslots for a technical deep-dive on Mon/Tue afternoon PT.

If that's agreeable, we can start the Hosted PoC as a low-risk first step while Marcus and Priyom scope the Dedicated migration lift.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0123

Date: Sat, 25 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo

Thanks Alex — good summary. Adding a few technical notes to set expectations and action items for the migration path choices:

- Model artifact compatibility: if you can provide weights in HF or PyTorch (.pt) we can run a direct conversion pipeline and test quantization. For custom operator forks we will need either source for the operator or to run inference in a containerized runtime on your Private deployment.

- KV/prefix cache: Hosted can emulate prefix cache behavior but the cold-starts will be higher than a colocated Dedicated pool. For 90 TPS with ~1k token seq lengths, we estimate median token latency on Hosted of ~120–180ms (depends on model size). Dedicated reduces variance and can hit 70–110ms median with proper batching.

- Fine-tuning: nightlies that push new weights can be handled with a blue/green rollout; the main lift is automating your training->artifact upload pipeline. If you require zero-downtime, plan for a short window (minutes) for KV warming after cutover.

Proposed phased plan (concrete):
1) Hosted smoke PoC (2 weeks): use a small distilled model or a snapshot of your model. Goals: latency baseline, end-to-end RAG verification, auth flow. Owner: Alex + Mina.
2) Dedicated sizing & soak (3–4 weeks): reserved GPU pool, run soak tests with synthetic bursts to validate autoscaling/burst behavior. Owner: Marcus + FinApps infra lead.
3) Private VPC prep (4–6 weeks parallel): network peering, KMS integration, and a dry-run deployment for compliance reviewers. Owner: Priyom + FinApps security.

Action items & deadlines:
- Alex: share model artifact or a 100M-parameter distilled variant (by 2026-10-26).
- Marcus: Dedicated capacity sketch & cost estimate (by 2026-10-27).
- Priyom: VPC checklist and KMS integration template (by 2026-10-29).

I'll put a short SOW-lite together once we confirm the PoC model — that'll outline the expected engineering time and any migration blockers. CC'ing Priyom for the VPC/compliance details.

Cheers,
Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

(212) 555-0146
